TotalEnergies Shares Methane Detection Expertise With Three National Oil Firms
sum: - SEA METEC support: TotalEnergies will share more than ten years of expertise from its TADI center to help develop SEA METEC.
- Sonangol agreement: A new memorandum of understanding expands methane and decarbonization cooperation in Angola.
- World Bank funding: The Angola partners will explore financing, including potential support from the World Bank’s GFMR Fund.

TotalEnergies has deepened methane partnerships with Petronas in Malaysia, Sonangol in Angola and Oil India (OIL). The European energy major will support the development of SEA METEC using expertise from its TotalEnergies Anomalies Detection Initiative (TADI) center. The partnerships aim to expand advanced methane detection and speed up emissions cuts.

TotalEnergies has built that expertise over more than ten years at TADI. According to the company, TADI is Europe’s only facility dedicated to evaluating methane detection and quantification technologies. SEA METEC is expected to strengthen knowledge sharing and help harmonize methane measurement and quantification methods. As a result, companies should be better able to detect, measure and ultimately curtail their emissions.

TotalEnergies linked the agreements to its commitment to the Oil & Gas Decarbonization Charter (OGDC). It did not disclose financial terms, timelines or details of its cooperation with OIL. “Our cooperation with Petronas in Malaysia, Sonangol in Angola and OIL in India illustrates TotalEnergies’ commitment to the OGDC and the momentum it has created among international and national companies,” said Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TotalEnergies. “I am convinced that by sharing technologies, expertise and best practices, we can accelerate concrete action and contribute to our common ambition of achieving near-zero upstream methane emissions by 2030,” Pouyanné added.

TotalEnergies has also signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Sonangol to strengthen technical cooperation in Angola. The agreement builds on experience gained through TotalEnergies’ AUSEA methane technology. It covers methane detection, measurement, monitoring and reduction, plus the sharing of best practices, methodologies and technical expertise.

TotalEnergies sees the agreements as a further step in strengthening its integrated gas position in Malaysia.

TotalEnergies (Paris:TTE) (LSE:TTE) (NYSE:TTE) announces the signing of agreements with PETRONAS Carigali Sdn Bhd (PCSB), PTTEP and KUFPEC to acquire a 30% operated interest in the Lang Lebah and B14 gas fields, located off the coast of Sarawak, Malaysia.

Lang Lebah, one of Malaysia’s largest offshore gas discoveries, and the nearby B14 field are planned to be developed as an integrated project. This combined development is expected to unlock more than 6.5 trillion cubic feet of gas resources (equivalent to more than 1 billion barrels of oil equivalent) to supply the existing Malaysia LNG liquefaction plant with a production plateau of around 10 billion cubic meters per annum (BCMA).

“The development of Lang Lebah and B14 resources will allow the creation of another large-scale gas hub in Malaysia, leveraging shared infrastructure, to supply gas to Malaysia LNG and meet the growing LNG demand in Asia,” said Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies. “These agreements mark another important step in our strategy to strengthen our integrated gas position in Malaysia, following the acquisition of SapuraOMV in 2024 and the expansion of our long-standing partnership with PETRONAS in 2025.”
Upon completion of the transactions, which are subject to regulatory approvals, TotalEnergies will hold a 30% operated interest in both fields, alongside PTTEP (25%), KUFPEC (25%) and PCSB (20%).

Namibian oil tycoon Knowledge Katti's Sintana Energy stake falls by $3.2 million
sum: The value of Namibian oil tycoon Knowledge Katti's stake in Sintana Energy Inc. has fallen by about C$4.5 million ($3.2 million) over the past year, as the Toronto-listed explorer's shares slid despite progress on its biggest asset, a stake in one of the largest oil discoveries off Namibia.

Katti, a Sintana director, owns 23.09 million shares in the company, or about 4.13%, according to the latest disclosure of his holdings. At Sintana's current price of 36 Canadian cents, the stake is worth about C$8.3 million ($5.9 million).

When Billionaires.Africa last valued his holding in August 2025, Katti owned 22.49 million shares and the stock traded at 57 Canadian cents, which put the stake at about C$12.8 million ($9.2 million). The shares have since fallen 37%. He owns about 600,000 more shares than he did then, but the extra holding has done little to offset the drop in price.

His percentage of the company has also shrunk, from 6.02% to 4.13%, because Sintana has issued a large number of new shares. Its share count has risen by about half in a year, to roughly 559 million, largely because of an all-share takeover. At the current price, Sintana has a market value of about C$201 million ($144 million).

The share issuance came mostly from Sintana's £45 million ($60 million) all-stock purchase of Challenger Energy Group, a London-listed explorer with offshore acreage in Uruguay. The deal closed in December 2025, and Sintana began trading on London's AIM market on Dec. 23, valued at about £128 million.

Challenger brought Sintana a stake in AREA OFF-1, an offshore block in Uruguay operated by Chevron Corp., which is paying the full cost of a 3D seismic survey there. The first season of the survey was completed earlier this year, and early results are expected in the second half of 2026.

Sintana has no revenue and reported losses as it waits for its partners to drill. Its shares had already lost more than 40% of their value in 2025 by early October, before the Challenger deal was completed.

TotalEnergies completes transfer of 10% Arctic LNG 2 stake to NordLine
sum: - Company retains rights to ~$1.3 billion in shareholder loan reimbursements
- Reimbursement implementation subject to applicable sanctions
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
TotalEnergies has completed the transfer of its 10% interest in the Arctic LNG 2 project to NordLine, a subsidiary of Novatek. The French energy major is no longer a shareholder in the venture.

The transaction was first mentioned during the presentation of the company's second quarter 2026 results. TotalEnergies confirmed the finalization of the deal, marking a full exit from the Russian-based liquefied natural gas project.

Under the terms of the transfer agreement, TotalEnergies retains specific financial rights related to the project's funding structure. The company holds the right to be reimbursed by Arctic LNG 2 for its share of loans provided by shareholders to the project.

The total value of these reimbursable loans stands at approximately $1.3 billion. TotalEnergies noted that any future implementation of such reimbursements will be subject to applicable sanctions regimes.

items.t: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Amazon.com, GE Aerospace and TotalEnergies
sum: Chicago, IL – October 23, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN, GE Aerospace GE and TotalEnergies SE TTE.
Top Research Reports for Amazon, GE Aerospace and TotalEnergies

The Zacks Research Daily presents the best research output of our analyst team. Today's Research Daily features new research reports on 16 major stocks, including Amazon.com, Inc., GE Aerospace and TotalEnergies SE. These research reports have been hand-picked from the roughly 70 reports published by our analyst team today.

Amazon's shares have outperformed the Zacks Internet - Commerce industry over the past year (+18.6% vs. +3.4%). The company's international expansion and diversification across e-commerce, AWS cloud services, advertising and streaming create multiple revenue streams while reducing concentration risk.

For the third quarter of 2026, Amazon guided net sales of $197-$202 billion and operating income of $22.5-$26.5 billion. AI integration across operations enhances personalization, logistics and AWS offerings, strengthening competitive positioning.

However, substantial capital expenditure requirements for AI infrastructure and data centers strain financial resources and compress margins, with trailing-12-month free cash outflow reported at $7.6 billion. The company's expanding debt burden reduces financial flexibility amid rising interest rates. Intensifying competition from Walmart, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud is an overhang.

Shares of GE Aerospace have declined -2.9% over the past year against the Zacks Aerospace - Defense industry's decline of -19.4%. The company is facing higher production costs, inflation and unfavorable product mix which could weigh on margins. Persistent supply-chain constraints may delay deliveries and increase expenses. The planned acquisition of Consolidated Precision Products could add debt and financing obligations.

items.t: UBS keeps EUR 89 target for TotalEnergies stock
sum: TotalEnergies (ISIN FR0000120271) traded at EUR 81.34 at Lang & Schwarz on October 22, 2026 at 11:07 a.m. CEST, 0.62 percent above the Xetra close of October 21, 2026 at EUR 80.84. UBS maintained its Buy rating and an EUR 89.00 target on October 21, 2026, according to MarketScreener.

The UBS target stands EUR 7.66 above the Lang & Schwarz price, a 9.42 percent premium calculated against EUR 81.34. The recommendation adds a current analyst reference before TotalEnergies publishes its third-quarter figures.

Second-quarter revenue was EUR 57.10 billion, compared with EUR 44.68 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. Net profit reached EUR 5.44 billion versus EUR 2.69 billion, according to Markets Insider.

On October 12, 2026, TotalEnergies began a share-purchase period that covered 2,529,480 shares at a weighted average price of EUR 79.805526, as Business Wire reported. On October 19, 2026, Jefferies raised its target from EUR 88.00 to EUR 90.00, according to Zonebourse. On October 21, 2026, UBS maintained its Buy rating and EUR 89.00 target.

TotalEnergies has scheduled its third-quarter 2026 results for October 29, 2026, with the press release at 7:00 a.m. London time and the presentation from 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. London time, according to the TotalEnergies results calendar. The scheduled release will provide the next test of the strong second-quarter comparison and the analyst targets now clustered above the current euro quote.

The stock traded at EUR 81.34 at Lang & Schwarz on October 22, 2026 at 11:07 a.m. CEST, 0.62 percent above the Xetra close of October 21, 2026 at EUR 80.84. The distance to the UBS target is 8.61 percent when measured from the current price. The further course of trading is shown by the continuously updated real-time quote of TotalEnergies stock.

sum: With an annual dividend yield of 5.43%, TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) is included among the 10 Energy Stocks with Highest Dividends.
TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) is a global integrated energy company that produces and markets energies.
On June 23, CICC initiated coverage of TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) with an 'Outperform' rating and a price target of €90, indicating an upside of over 32% from the current levels.

TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) raised its dividend and doubled its share buybacks in April after its earnings topped expectations in the first quarter, driven by the Middle East war-driven oil rally. The French energy major announced a 5.9% dividend increase and authorized stock buybacks of up to $1.5 billion for the second quarter, compared to the $750 million target for Q1 announced in February.
This marks a sharp turnaround as TotalEnergies slowed buybacks and announced a cost-savings programme late last year, forecasting that the already low oil prices would fall further.
Antipodes Global Strategy stated the following regarding TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) in its Q1 2026 investor letter:

"TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) surged higher towards the end of the Quarter supported by volatile and elevated oil prices, which lifted earnings expectations and cash flow outlook. Heightened geopolitical tensions drove sharp swings in Brent Crude, benefiting integrated energy producers with strong upstream leverage. The rally was reinforced by solid CY25 results and constructive 2026 guidance, including expected production growth, rising LNG volumes and continued expansion in integrated power, which further underpinned investor confidence."
